messages:
maria: Heads up — since ~22:12 UTC we're seeing a sharp IOPS spike on /scratch in us-west2 that is causing GPU node attaches to hang. Pods Pending with AttachTimeout.
raj: Confirming, saw a bunch of kubelet errors: 'attach/detach timeout' and then gpu-allocator backoff. Multiple AZs in the region affected.
zach: infra-bot fired storage_iops_spike alert for us-west2-scratchpool at 22:14. Link: https://ops/alerts/1755007777 (signal: sustained 90% io_util over baseline) :rotating_light:
maria: Quick paste of iostat from one affected host (trimmed):
```
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00 5.00 10.00 400.00 512.00 20480.00 50.00 6.20 14.00 0.80 14.20 0.45 96.00
```
kai: avgqu-sz=6.2 and %util 96% — that's brutal. Any concurrent janitor/scrub jobs?
maria: Yes, we rotated a new janitor policy last night increasing aggressive parallelism for tempfile sweep in scratchpool. Change landed in config at 03:00 local, might correlate.
raj: Can we throttle the janitor QPS quickly? I'm on it. If we reduce concurrency we should relieve the queue length and let attaches proceed.
infra-bot: automated action: scaling down scratch-janitor concurrency from 12 -> 4 for us-west2 at 22:28 UTC.
zach: Noted ephemeral cleaner scaled down. Watching metrics — iops trend shows a gradual decline but still noisy.
maria: Workaround applied: pinned new GPU attach jobs to nodes with separate nvme (scratch-isolated) via nodeSelector, reduced pending by ~60%. Temporary but helpful.
kai: For a longer fix we should revert aggressive janitor parallelism and run a canary with lower qps, and update deploy rollback doc. I'll open PR for policy rollback.
raj: Also we should add a circuit-breaker so future janitor config changes auto-scale down if iops_util > 80% for > 5m. Filing follow-up ticket.
oncall-rotation: @maria @kai can you pair on the rollback and post the minimal repro steps? I'll document the incident notes for the oncall handover.
maria: Will do. Minimal repro: run the tempfile sweep with concurrency 12 on a large scratchpool dataset (50M files) while launching 20 concurrent GPU attach jobs — you will see avgqu increase and kubelet attach timeouts.
zach: After scale-down to 4 we still saw intermittent checksum errors on two hosts — suspect transient read retries. I've captured smartctl logs and saved to /var/logs/scratch-iops/1755007777/ for postmortem.
kai: Adding storage team to postmortem. Action items: 1) rollback janitor policy, 2) add iops-based safety throttle, 3) run targeted fio workload to characterize threshold, 4) verify firmware on nvme fleet for read-retry anomalies.
oncall-rotation: Thanks team. Leaving note: oncall to monitor us-west2 for next 6 hours and escalate if %util > 85% persists. :thumbsup:
